evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.read_only_scope: data/** and docs/math-foundations.md only; src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, git history and the diff were never opened

sources.note: A rechargeRate with a CDR-immune cooldown is the ammo/charge shape: the ability stocks charges on a 7 s timer rather than gating on a single cooldown.

modeled = SLOTS keys incl. synthetic Q2 (2nd charge) ... "ammo (Q 2nd charge at 40 splinters)"
sources.note: Confirms the second Dark Sphere charge is a first-class, separately-nameable slot (Q2) in the Syndra contract, not an implicit repeat of Q.

sources.quote: splinters option: 120 -> 1.15x AP buff, 40+ Q charges via Q2 slot, 60+ W true damage

Ability recasts are scheduled on one shared timeline (the champion has one set of hands): each cast occupies its sourced cast time, an ability recasts when its effective cooldown has elapsed and no other cast is in progress, and a cast counts when it starts within the window (_schedule_shared_casts) ... the shared-timeline version is the superposition with mutual-exclusion, resolved greedily by cast order.
sources.note: The timeline is ordered by cast order over slots; a legal slot in the supplied order occupies its own timeline index.

sources.quote: The event order shown in the UI comes from the fight's cast_order + breakdown damage_events. ... a rotation resolver ... computes the fight's cast_order from the champion's atomized data + the combo table, replacing the naive DEFAULT_CAST_ORDER when a combo exists.
sources.note: Establishes that a 'custom order' scenario supplies an explicit cast_order over slot ids, and that cast_timeline entries are that order's slots in sequence.

independent_computation.step_1_what_the_scenario_parameter_60_is: Syndra's Transcendent (P) thresholds in the cached wiki text are 40 (Q second charge, S2), 60 (W bonus true damage, S5), 80 (E scatter/slow), 100 (R execute), 120 (P +15% AP). The champion contract exposes exactly one integer knob over that range - 'splinters option (0-120)' (S7, S8). A Syndra scenario suffixed _60 therefore denotes splinters = 60, the W true-damage threshold; 60 is a named splinter gate for Syndra and matches no other Syndra parameter in the cached data.
independent_computation.step_2_charge_availability: Charge gate from S2: charges_available = 2 if splinters >= 40 else 1. With splinters = 60: 60 >= 40 -> TRUE, so Syndra holds up to 2 stocked Dark Sphere charges. S3 confirms the stocking mechanism (rechargeRate 7 s per charge, base cooldown flagged not-affected-by-CDR, i.e. ammo semantics, not a single-cooldown ability), and S4 confirms the charges are a visible, countable resource once the Transcendent bonus is active.
independent_computation.step_3_back_to_back_legality: Because a second charge is stocked, a second Dark Sphere cast may follow the first immediately - it does not wait 7 s. Under the shared-timeline rule (S9) the only constraint on the next cast is that no other cast is in progress; Syndra's Q has castTime 'none' in the cache, so the second charge occupies the next timeline index directly after the first Dark Sphere.
independent_computation.step_4_index_1_identity: The scenario is a custom-cast-order scenario (S10): the timeline is the supplied slot order in sequence. Syndra's slot set includes the synthetic Q2 = 'second Dark Sphere charge' (S7, S8) alongside Q, W, E, R. A custom order authored at splinters = 60 exercises exactly the two bonuses live at 60 - the Q second charge (>=40) and W's true damage (>=60) - so the natural order is Q, Q2, W, E, R. Index 0 = Dark Sphere, index 1 = Q2 = the second stocked charge, index 2 = Force of Will.
independent_computation.step_5_diagnosis_of_the_old_value: The old leaf value 'Force of Will' at index 1 is what the timeline degrades to when the Q2 slot is dropped from the supplied order and every later entry shifts up one index: Q, [Q2 dropped], W -> index 1 = W = 'Force of Will'. Dropping Q2 at splinters = 60 contradicts S2 directly (the charge unlocks at 40, and 60 >= 40). No reading of the cached wiki text withholds the second charge at 60 splinters.
independent_computation.step_6_label_check: The new label's two components are both sourced: 'Dark Sphere' is the verbatim ability name (S1), and '(2nd charge)' is the wiki's own charge framing - 'stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2' (S2) with the per-charge count shown in-client (S4). A bare 'Dark Sphere' would be ambiguous with index 0; the disambiguating suffix is correct and matches the contract's own naming of the slot as the 2nd charge (S7).
independent_computation.conclusion: At splinters = 60 Syndra has 2 Dark Sphere charges, so the second Dark Sphere cast is a legal, distinct timeline entry immediately after the first. cast_timeline[1].name = 'Dark Sphere (2nd charge)'. The new value is correct; the old value is the symptom of the Q2 entry being omitted and Force of Will shifting from index 2 to index 1.

arithmetic.splinter_gate_Q_second_charge: threshold 40; scenario 60; 60 - 40 = +20 over the gate -> charges = 2
arithmetic.splinter_gate_W_true_damage: threshold 60; scenario 60; 60 - 60 = 0, gate met (met-at-equality is why the scenario is pinned at exactly 60)
arithmetic.charge_recharge: 7 s per stocked charge, cooldown.affectedByCdr = false -> the 2nd charge is already banked at fight start and imposes no wait before index 1

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition itself lives in scripts/ or tests/, which this runbook forbids reading, so the supplied cast order was inferred rather than read. The inference rests on: (a) 'custom_order' meaning an author-supplied order over slot ids (S10); (b) Q2 being a real slot id in Syndra's contract (S7, S8); and (c) an engine not inventing casts absent from a custom order, so a slot can only appear at index 1 if the author placed it there. The mechanical fact that is fully independent of the scenario file - that a second Dark Sphere charge is available and castable at 60 splinters (S2, S3) - is the load-bearing one, and it is what makes the new value admissible and the old value's omission a defect.
